h1: Failure to Appear Defense Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: Missing the court date on a traffic ticket creates a second criminal charge — failure to appear under Transportation Code 543.009 — stacked on top of the original citation. Attorney Robert Navar resolves both cases together, often with neither one becoming a conviction.
summary: Failure to appear (FTA, sometimes called VPTA) is a separate Class C misdemeanor in Texas, filed by the court when you miss the appearance date on a citation. You now have two cases, not one.
An FTA charge usually comes with an arrest warrant and a report to DPS that blocks your license renewal until both cases are cleared.
Both cases are handled together: we get the warrant recalled, then work for a dismissal or deferred disposition on the original ticket and the FTA so neither goes on your record.

Common defenses include never receiving notice, a wrong address on the citation, or a court error. Our flat fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in JP and area city courts, plus $35 for the first warrant.

sections.heading: What Failure to Appear Means on a Texas Traffic Ticket
paragraphs: When an El Paso officer hands you a citation, you sign a written promise to appear in court by a certain date. Texas Transportation Code 543.009 makes breaking that promise its own offense — a Class C misdemeanor called failure to appear, or "violate promise to appear" (VPTA) on some court dockets. It carries its own fine, up to $200 plus court costs, and it is filed whether the original ticket was for speeding, no insurance or a expired registration.

The practical effect is that one ticket becomes two cases with two cause numbers. In El Paso Municipal Court you will see them listed separately on the warrant list, each with its own fine and its own warrant. If you were cited for three violations at one stop and missed the date, you may now be looking at six cases.

Many clients find out about the FTA charge months or years later — when they try to renew a license, when a background check turns it up, or when a routine stop on I-10 ends in an arrest. The charge does not expire, and neither does the warrant.

sections.heading: The Warrant and the OMNI Report That Follow
paragraphs: Two things happen behind the scenes once an FTA is filed. First, the judge signs a warrant on the original ticket and often a second warrant on the FTA charge. Second, the court reports you to the Texas Department of Public Safety under the Failure to Appear program in Transportation Code Chapter 706 — the OMNI hold. DPS will not renew your driver's license until the court sends a clearance, and each case carries a $10 OMNI fee that must be paid before the clearance goes out.

This is why an FTA is worse than the ticket itself. The ticket was a fine. The FTA adds a second fine, an arrest warrant, a license hold, and the cost of untangling all of it. The good news is that the same attorney appearance that gets the warrant recalled also puts the FTA on a pretrial docket where it can be negotiated like any other Class C case.

sections.heading: How We Resolve the Original Ticket and the FTA Together
paragraphs: Once you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance on every open cause number — the ticket and the FTA — and request that each warrant be recalled. In El Paso Municipal Court that typically happens within 24–48 hours. The court then resets everything to a single pretrial setting where Robert Navar meets with the prosecutor.

Our goal on the FTA charge is a dismissal, and prosecutors in El Paso frequently agree to dismiss it when the underlying ticket is being resolved and the client has no pattern of missed dates. On the original citation we work for the same outcomes we pursue on any ticket: an outright dismissal, deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051, or, where the judge allows it, a driving safety course dismissal.
You do not attend the pretrial. In most cases the first time you hear from us after hiring is to tell you the warrants are gone, and the second is to tell you how both cases ended.

sections.heading: Defenses to a Failure to Appear Charge
paragraphs: Failure to appear is not automatic just because a date passed. The State must show you knowingly failed to appear, and in El Paso we see the same fact patterns over and over that undercut that element. The most common: the citation listed an old address, the court mailed a reset notice that never arrived, the officer wrote an appearance date that fell on a weekend or court holiday, or the client was deployed from Fort Bliss, hospitalized, or in custody elsewhere on the date.

Court error happens too. Payments get posted to the wrong cause number, a defensive-driving request gets lost, or a case the client thought was closed is reopened for a missing certificate. When we pull the court's file we are looking for exactly these gaps, and when we find one we present it to the prosecutor as the reason the FTA should be dismissed outright rather than deferred.

Even without a clean defense, the FTA is a fine-only Class C case in a court that sees thousands of them. Judges and prosecutors care far more about resolving the underlying ticket than punishing a missed date, which gives an attorney real room to negotiate.

sections.heading: Failure to Appear in JP, Horizon City, Socorro and Area Courts
paragraphs: The rules are the same across El Paso County, but the practice differs. The Justice of the Peace precincts handle FTAs on Sheriff's, constable and DPS trooper tickets; Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton each have their own judge, docket day and habits about dismissing FTAs. Our flat fee in those courts is $69 per ticket, plus the same $35 / $20 warrant add-on.

Because an FTA in one court can sit beside an older one in another, we start every case with a county-wide check. Our free ticket and warrant lookup finds each open case and tells you the court, the charges and the total fee before you pay anything. Se habla español.

sections.heading: What Not to Do After Missing a Court Date
paragraphs: Do not pay the ticket online to make it go away. Paying is a guilty plea; it puts a conviction on your DPS record, and it usually does not clear the separate FTA case or the OMNI hold. Do not go to the courthouse window without a lawyer, because an active warrant can be served there.
Call us or submit the lookup form, and we will tell you exactly what is open and how to close it. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: Is failure to appear a criminal charge in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Transportation Code 543.009 it is a Class C misdemeanor, the same level as the traffic ticket itself. It is fine-only, but it is a separate case with its own cause number, its own fine and, usually, its own warrant.

faqs.q: If I pay the original ticket, does the failure to appear charge go away?
faqs.a: Usually not. The FTA is its own case and must be resolved separately. Paying the ticket also enters a conviction on your record, which is the opposite of what we want. Let us handle both cases together on one docket.

faqs.q: Can a failure to appear be dismissed?
faqs.a: Often, yes. El Paso prosecutors routinely dismiss the FTA when the underlying ticket is being resolved through dismissal or deferred disposition, and especially when there is a notice problem such as a wrong address. We ask for that dismissal on every FTA we handle.

faqs.q: Will a failure to appear show up on a background check?
faqs.a: An open FTA with a warrant can appear on background checks and will block your license renewal through OMNI. Once dismissed or deferred and completed, the case may be eligible for expunction under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 55A.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to fix a failure to appear in El Paso?
faqs.a: Our fee is $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court or $69 in JP and area city courts, plus $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one. Court fees, if any, depend on the outcome. Consultations are free.

faqs.q: I never got a court date. Do I still have an FTA?
faqs.a: Possibly. Courts file FTAs based on the date on the citation, not on whether you received a reminder. If the citation had a wrong address or the date was never communicated, that is a real defense, and we raise it. Start with the free lookup so we can see what the court filed.
